title: Laboratory Quality Systems (ISO & GLP)
source_note: Grounded in standard laboratory quality management content: ISO/IEC 17025, ISO 15189, Good Laboratory Practice (GLP) principles, quality control/assurance, accreditation, audits, document control, proficiency testing, and measurement uncertainty, at the 400 level.

questions.question: What does the acronym GLP stand for in laboratory quality contexts?
options: Good Laboratory Practice
General Laboratory Protocol
Grouped Laboratory Personnel
Global Laboratory Program
questions.correct_answer: Good Laboratory Practice
questions.explanation: GLP stands for Good Laboratory Practice, a quality system of management controls for non-clinical safety studies to ensure data integrity and reliability.

questions.question: What is the primary purpose of Good Laboratory Practice (GLP) principles?
options: To ensure the quality, reliability, and integrity of non-clinical laboratory study data
To increase laboratory profit margins
To reduce the number of staff required in a laboratory
To eliminate the need for equipment calibration
questions.correct_answer: To ensure the quality, reliability, and integrity of non-clinical laboratory study data
questions.explanation: GLP establishes a framework of organizational processes and conditions to ensure consistent, high-quality, and traceable study data.

questions.question: Under GLP, who holds ultimate responsibility for the overall conduct of a study?
options: The Study Director
The receptionist
The equipment vendor
The patient
questions.correct_answer: The Study Director
questions.explanation: GLP designates the Study Director as the single point of control responsible for the overall conduct and reporting of a non-clinical study.

questions.question: What role does the Quality Assurance Unit (QAU) play under GLP?
options: It independently monitors and audits study conduct to verify compliance with GLP and the protocol
It performs the actual laboratory experiments
It sets the price of laboratory tests
It replaces the Study Director's responsibilities
questions.correct_answer: It independently monitors and audits study conduct to verify compliance with GLP and the protocol
questions.explanation: The QAU operates independently from the study team, auditing processes and records to ensure compliance with GLP principles and study protocols.

questions.question: What is ISO/IEC 17025 primarily concerned with?
options: General requirements for the competence of testing and calibration laboratories
Requirements for environmental management systems
Requirements for food safety management
Requirements for occupational health and safety only
questions.correct_answer: General requirements for the competence of testing and calibration laboratories
questions.explanation: ISO/IEC 17025 specifies general requirements for the competence, impartiality, and consistent operation of testing and calibration laboratories.

questions.question: Which ISO standard is specifically tailored to the quality and competence requirements of medical laboratories?
options: ISO 17025 only, with no medical-specific standard
questions.explanation: ISO 15189 addresses quality and competence specifically for medical laboratories, incorporating both management and technical requirements relevant to patient testing.

questions.question: What is the difference between accreditation and certification for a laboratory?
options: Accreditation formally recognizes technical competence to perform specific tests; certification confirms conformance to a management system standard
They are identical processes with no distinction
Certification always requires more technical evidence than accreditation
Accreditation only applies to research, never diagnostic, laboratories
questions.correct_answer: Accreditation formally recognizes technical competence to perform specific tests; certification confirms conformance to a management system standard
questions.explanation: Accreditation (e.g., to ISO 17025/15189) confirms technical competence for specific tests, while certification (e.g., ISO 9001) confirms a management system meets a standard, without necessarily assessing technical testing competence.

questions.question: What is the purpose of an internal audit in a laboratory quality management system?
options: To systematically review whether the laboratory's processes conform to its own quality system and relevant standards
To determine staff salary increments
To replace external accreditation assessments entirely
To design new laboratory tests
questions.correct_answer: To systematically review whether the laboratory's processes conform to its own quality system and relevant standards
questions.explanation: Internal audits are planned, periodic self-assessments to verify that the laboratory's activities comply with its documented quality management system and applicable standards.

questions.question: What distinguishes an external audit from an internal audit?
options: An external audit is conducted by an independent body outside the laboratory, such as an accreditation body
An external audit is always less rigorous than an internal audit
An external audit is performed only by laboratory staff
There is no meaningful difference
questions.correct_answer: An external audit is conducted by an independent body outside the laboratory, such as an accreditation body
questions.explanation: External audits are conducted by independent external parties (e.g., accreditation bodies) to objectively assess compliance, unlike internal audits performed by the laboratory's own staff.

questions.question: What is a 'non-conformance' in the context of a laboratory quality management system?
options: A deviation from established procedures, standards, or requirements
A correctly followed test procedure
A staff member's annual leave request
A newly purchased piece of equipment
questions.correct_answer: A deviation from established procedures, standards, or requirements
questions.explanation: A non-conformance is any failure to meet specified requirements, procedures, or standards, requiring investigation and corrective action.

questions.question: What is the purpose of Corrective and Preventive Action (CAPA) in a quality system?
options: To eliminate the cause of existing non-conformances and prevent potential future occurrences
To punish staff responsible for errors
To increase the number of tests performed
To reduce the accuracy requirements of tests
questions.correct_answer: To eliminate the cause of existing non-conformances and prevent potential future occurrences
questions.explanation: CAPA processes address the root causes of identified problems (corrective) and proactively reduce the risk of similar future problems (preventive).

questions.question: What is proficiency testing (PT) also known as in laboratory quality assurance?
options: External Quality Assessment (EQA)
Internal Quality Control (IQC)
Standard Operating Procedure (SOP)
Document control
questions.correct_answer: External Quality Assessment (EQA)
questions.explanation: Proficiency testing, also called External Quality Assessment, involves comparing a laboratory's results on blind samples against other participating laboratories or a reference value.

questions.question: What action should a laboratory take if it receives an unsatisfactory proficiency testing result?
options: Investigate the root cause and implement corrective action before reporting further patient results affected by the issue
Ignore the result if only one test was affected
Immediately close the laboratory permanently
Report the unsatisfactory result as satisfactory
questions.correct_answer: Investigate the root cause and implement corrective action before reporting further patient results affected by the issue
questions.explanation: An unsatisfactory PT result requires investigation into potential causes (e.g., reagent, calibration, technique) and corrective action to restore confidence in test accuracy.

questions.question: What is 'measurement uncertainty' in the context of laboratory testing?
options: A quantified estimate of the doubt or range associated with a measured value
The name of a staff performance metric
A term used only in qualitative research
The list of equipment brands used
questions.correct_answer: A quantified estimate of the doubt or range associated with a measured value
questions.explanation: Measurement uncertainty is a parameter that characterizes the dispersion of values that could reasonably be attributed to a measured quantity, reflecting confidence in the result.

questions.question: Why is estimating measurement uncertainty important for accredited testing laboratories?
options: It helps assess the reliability and comparability of reported results, as required by standards like ISO 17025
It has no practical importance
It is used to set staff salaries
It replaces the need for calibration
questions.correct_answer: It helps assess the reliability and comparability of reported results, as required by standards like ISO 17025
questions.explanation: Reporting measurement uncertainty allows users to judge the reliability of results and is a formal requirement under standards like ISO/IEC 17025.

questions.question: What is the purpose of a document control system in a quality management framework?
options: To ensure only current, approved versions of documents are used and obsolete ones are withdrawn
To track staff working hours
To eliminate the need for record keeping
To manage laboratory finances
questions.correct_answer: To ensure only current, approved versions of documents are used and obsolete ones are withdrawn
questions.explanation: Document control ensures staff always use the latest approved version of SOPs, forms, and policies, preventing errors from outdated documentation.

questions.question: What is meant by 'traceability' in a laboratory quality system?
options: The ability to trace a measurement result back through a documented chain of calibrations to a recognized standard
The ability to track staff attendance
The color-coding of laboratory reagents
The physical location of the laboratory building
questions.correct_answer: The ability to trace a measurement result back through a documented chain of calibrations to a recognized standard
questions.explanation: Metrological traceability links a measurement result through an unbroken chain of calibrations to a recognized reference standard, ensuring comparability of results.

questions.question: What is the purpose of retaining laboratory records, raw data, and specimens under GLP requirements?
options: To allow reconstruction of the study and verification of reported findings at a later date
To reduce laboratory storage costs
Record retention is not required under GLP
To discard records immediately after reporting
questions.correct_answer: To allow reconstruction of the study and verification of reported findings at a later date
questions.explanation: GLP requires archiving of raw data, records, and specimens for a defined period, enabling later reconstruction and verification of study conduct and results.

questions.question: What does a Standard Operating Procedure (SOP) primarily achieve within a quality system?
options: Consistency and standardization of how a specific task or test is performed by all staff
Automatic equipment repair
Elimination of the need for staff competency assessment
Automatic accreditation of the laboratory
questions.correct_answer: Consistency and standardization of how a specific task or test is performed by all staff
questions.explanation: SOPs provide detailed, standardized instructions ensuring that a procedure is performed the same way regardless of who carries it out.

questions.question: What is a 'quality manual' in a laboratory's quality management system?
options: A top-level document describing the laboratory's quality policy, scope, and structure of the quality system
A user manual for a single piece of equipment
A list of staff phone numbers
A patient information leaflet
questions.correct_answer: A top-level document describing the laboratory's quality policy, scope, and structure of the quality system
questions.explanation: The quality manual is the overarching document outlining the laboratory's quality policy, objectives, and the structure of its management system.

questions.question: What is the purpose of a Levey-Jennings chart in laboratory internal quality control?
options: To graphically monitor control results over time and detect trends or shifts indicating loss of test precision/accuracy
To schedule staff shifts
To track reagent purchase orders
To record patient demographic data
questions.correct_answer: To graphically monitor control results over time and detect trends or shifts indicating loss of test precision/accuracy
questions.explanation: A Levey-Jennings chart plots QC results against time with control limits, allowing visual detection of trends, shifts, or out-of-control results.

questions.question: In quality control, what do the Westgard rules primarily help laboratories determine?
options: Whether a QC run should be accepted or rejected based on statistical patterns of control results
The correct sample volume for a test
The staff duty roster
The reagent expiry date
questions.correct_answer: Whether a QC run should be accepted or rejected based on statistical patterns of control results
questions.explanation: Westgard rules are a set of statistical decision criteria applied to QC data to decide whether an analytical run is in control (acceptable) or out of control (rejected).

questions.question: What is the difference between 'accuracy' and 'precision' in laboratory measurement?
options: Accuracy is closeness to the true value; precision is the closeness of repeated measurements to each other
Accuracy and precision mean exactly the same thing
Precision refers only to equipment cost
Accuracy applies only to qualitative tests
questions.correct_answer: Accuracy is closeness to the true value; precision is the closeness of repeated measurements to each other
questions.explanation: Accuracy reflects how close a measured value is to the true/reference value, while precision reflects the reproducibility/consistency of repeated measurements.

questions.question: What is meant by 'method validation' before a new test is introduced into routine laboratory use?
options: Confirming through objective evidence that the method reliably produces accurate, reproducible results for its intended use
Simply reading the manufacturer's instructions
Skipping verification if the kit is imported
Validating only the cost of the test
questions.correct_answer: Confirming through objective evidence that the method reliably produces accurate, reproducible results for its intended use
questions.explanation: Method validation provides documented evidence that a test method performs as intended, meeting accuracy, precision, and other performance requirements before clinical use.

questions.question: Which of the following is typically assessed during method verification/validation?
options: Precision, accuracy, linearity, and reportable range of the method
Only the color of the reagent bottle
Only the manufacturer's marketing claims
Only the cost per test
questions.correct_answer: Precision, accuracy, linearity, and reportable range of the method
questions.explanation: Method validation typically evaluates performance characteristics such as precision, accuracy, linearity, and the analytically reportable range.

questions.question: What is the purpose of a Quality Policy statement in a laboratory?
options: To declare management's commitment to quality and the framework for setting quality objectives
To set the price of laboratory tests
To describe the laboratory's building layout
To list staff annual leave dates
questions.correct_answer: To declare management's commitment to quality and the framework for setting quality objectives
questions.explanation: A quality policy is a formal statement from top management expressing commitment to quality and providing a framework for setting and reviewing quality objectives.

questions.question: What does 'impartiality' mean as a requirement for accredited testing laboratories under ISO/IEC 17025?
options: Laboratory activities and results must be free from undue influence, conflicts of interest, or bias
The laboratory must never report any results
Impartiality is a term unrelated to laboratory accreditation
All staff must have identical qualifications
questions.correct_answer: Laboratory activities and results must be free from undue influence, conflicts of interest, or bias
questions.explanation: Impartiality requires that laboratory activities are undertaken objectively, without conflicts of interest or bias compromising the results.

questions.question: What is a 'management review' in the context of a laboratory quality management system?
options: A periodic top-management evaluation of the quality system's suitability, adequacy, and effectiveness
A daily staff attendance check
A one-time review conducted only before accreditation
A financial audit unrelated to quality
questions.correct_answer: A periodic top-management evaluation of the quality system's suitability, adequacy, and effectiveness
questions.explanation: Management review is a scheduled evaluation by senior leadership of the quality system's performance, using inputs like audit results and complaints to drive improvement.

questions.question: What is the purpose of a 'chain of custody' record for forensic or legal laboratory samples?
options: To document every individual who handled the sample, ensuring its integrity and admissibility as evidence
To record the reagents used in a test
To calculate laboratory turnaround time
To track staff vacation requests
questions.correct_answer: To document every individual who handled the sample, ensuring its integrity and admissibility as evidence
questions.explanation: Chain of custody documentation tracks every person who has handled a sample from collection to analysis, ensuring evidentiary integrity, especially important in forensic contexts.

questions.question: What is the purpose of retaining a 'Quality Assurance Statement' with a GLP study's final report?
options: To confirm the QAU independently reviewed and audited the study for compliance with GLP
To list the study budget
To provide the study director's personal biography
To replace the raw data of the study
questions.correct_answer: To confirm the QAU independently reviewed and audited the study for compliance with GLP
questions.explanation: The QA statement, signed by the QAU, confirms that the study was inspected and audited to verify adherence to GLP principles, lending credibility to the final report.

questions.question: In laboratory quality systems, what is a 'complaint' handling procedure meant to ensure?
options: That client or stakeholder complaints are systematically recorded, investigated, and resolved
That complaints are automatically dismissed
That only verbal complaints are considered valid
That complaints are handled without any documentation
questions.correct_answer: That client or stakeholder complaints are systematically recorded, investigated, and resolved
questions.explanation: A formal complaint-handling procedure ensures complaints are logged, investigated for root cause, and resolved appropriately, feeding into continual improvement.

questions.question: What is 'continual improvement' as a principle of laboratory quality management systems?
options: An ongoing effort to enhance processes, products, or services based on data such as audits, QC, and feedback
A one-time upgrade of laboratory equipment
A requirement only for newly accredited laboratories
A concept unrelated to ISO standards
questions.correct_answer: An ongoing effort to enhance processes, products, or services based on data such as audits, QC, and feedback
questions.explanation: Continual improvement is a core quality management principle involving the ongoing use of data (audits, QC trends, complaints) to progressively enhance laboratory performance.
